producer_report.summary: The baseline lookup now waits for main's run when it is still in progress. Right after a landing, main's run for the base's content is usually still going. The old lookup made one read, found it unfinished, and fell back to a 20-minute local run. In `run/checks.rs`, `green_run` takes a `wait_s` argument. The main-tip lookup passes `ctx.jc.config.budget.ci_wait_s`, and the landed-candidate lookup passes 0, so it stays one read. A new `WaitsWhileRunning` source replaces `RunsOnly`. It reports an absent run as an error until a read has shown the run in progress, so a run that never appeared is not waited for, because the read loop treats an error as "no result". Reads, 20 s pauses and the bound come from `with_ci_source_on`, `Paced`, `routing::ci_polls` and `CI_POLL`. No new limit, key or config was added. The doc comments on `take_baseline`, `reused_baseline` and `green_run` no longer say "no wait". In `run/tests.rs`, `CiReplies` gained `in_progress_first(n)`, which answers in-progress for the first n reads of the matching run. A `current` cell keeps the jobs listing in step with the run reply. There are four new tests. They drive the real `go` path and fake only `gh` and the sleeper. `CHANGELOG.md` has an entry under [Unreleased] / Changed. I did not run the full suite or the new tests against the pre-change source.

learnings: `Paced` sleeps before every read after its first, and `with_ci_source_on` builds a new `Paced` per call. So each lookup restarts its pacing, and a Missing candidate run in tests adds 75 pauses of 20 s after the baseline's.
`read_ci` treats a fetch `Err` as Missing and stops, but treats `Ok(None)` and unfinished as 'keep polling to the bound'. That is the lever used to avoid waiting on an absent run.
`CiReplies` gets run and jobs answers from separate requests, so a mode that changes the reply per read must record the current reply for the jobs listing.
Bash in this role cannot pipe to `tail`; run cargo commands bare.
